documents.unit: Center for Innovation in Teaching and Learning (CITL)
documents.title: Generative AI Syllabus Statements
documents.stance_why: The page offers three template statements (open, moderate, closed) and says 'faculty may have different expectations for the use of AI', leaving the choice to instructors. A document offering tiers or templates is coded delegates.
tiers: Open Use: Permitted in this Course with Attribution
Moderate Use: Permitted when Assigned in this Course with Attribution
Closed: Not Permitted in this Course
documents.summary: Teaching-center page giving faculty three ready-to-paste syllabus statements, from open use with attribution to a closed ban treated as misconduct. It also warns users not to share sensitive data with AI tools.

units.why: The page frames the statements as options for faculty, with expectations varying by course: 'faculty may have different expectations for the use of AI'. The decision is left to each instructor, so P04.
units.anchor: Depending on the course, faculty may have different expectations for the use of AI.
units.frag_start: Depending on the course, faculty
units.frag_end: expectations for the use of AI.

units.why: A recommendation to instructors to make AI expectations explicit in courses: 'We recommend clearly outlining when and how students should use these tools'. It is a syllabus-communication rule (P09), not a mandate, so modality should.
units.anchor: We recommend clearly outlining when and how students should use these tools within your courses.
units.frag_start: We recommend clearly outlining when
units.fit_note: A recommendation, not a requirement, to state AI expectations.

units.why: The page offers ready-made statements to paste into the syllabus template; this is the three-option menu of open, moderate and closed use. Tiers go under P05; the 'few options' wording shows the tiers are templates for instructors.
units.anchor: Below you will find a few options for statements that can be added to the
units.frag_start: Below you will find a few
units.policy: CITL offers a few alternative AI syllabus statements that instructors can add to the standard course syllabus template or their own syllabi.

units.why: Warns that AI tools may use input data for training, so 'the confidentiality of the information you provide is not guaranteed'. This is a privacy caution for all users (P50).
units.anchor: the confidentiality of the information you provide is not guaranteed
units.frag_start: user data provided can be utilized
units.policy: When using AI tools, user data provided can be used for training AI models or other purposes, so the confidentiality of the information provided is not guaranteed.

units.why: Directs faculty and students to refrain from sharing sensitive data: 'refrain from sharing any sensitive or private data'. A conduct rule on data protection, P50 (protect personal data); it names PII, PHI, financial data, IP.
units.anchor: refrain from sharing any sensitive or private data while using these tools
units.frag_start: Faculty and students should be mindful
units.fit_note: Also lists intellectual property and legally protected data among the types not to share.

units.why: Defines the open tier: 'AI is allowed to be used throughout the course' with citation and attribution. Naming a tier is P05; its stance is permissive with conditions.
units.anchor: AI is allowed to be used throughout the course so long as it is done
units.frag_start: AI is allowed to be used
units.fit_note: Also the permissive-with-attribution default of the open tier (P02).

units.why: The open-tier statement says AI is 'encouraged to be used by students with the purpose of supporting their work'. That is an encouraging default stance for courses that adopt it (P02).
units.anchor: Generative AI resources are encouraged to be used by students with the purpose of supporting
units.frag_start: Generative AI resources are encouraged

units.why: The open and moderate statements both require disclosure: 'students must openly disclose any AI-generated material they utilize and provide proper attribution'. Disclosure with each submission is P24.
units.anchor: students must openly disclose any AI-generated material they utilize and provide proper attribution.

units.why: Specifies the form of attribution: 'in-text citations, quotations, and references'. This names the citation format, close to P25, but without tool/prompt details, so partial fit.
units.anchor: This includes in-text citations, quotations, and references.
units.frag_start: This includes in-text citations
units.fit_note: Specifies citation forms (in-text, quotations, references) rather than tool or prompt details.

units.why: Supplies a model acknowledgment naming the tool, provider and manner of use: 'The author(s) acknowledge the utilization of [Generative AI Tool Name]'. Requiring tool, provider and how it was used is P25.

units.policy: A student includes in assignments an acknowledgment naming the Generative AI tool, its provider, and the manner(s) in which it was used.

units.why: Points students to citation guidelines hosted by CITL: 'Proper citation guidelines can be found on the CITL website'. It directs to support resources (P72 human help is not exact); it fits no type well, so UNCOVERED.

units.why: Defines the moderate tier: AI 'permitted for specific assignments or within set parameters by the instructor'. Naming a tier is P05, and the per-assignment choice is also instructor-set.
units.anchor: AI is permitted for specific assignments or within set parameters by the instructor.

units.why: Defines the closed tier: 'AI is not permitted for any use within this course'. A default ban on all AI in the course, P01; also names a tier.
units.anchor: AI is not permitted for any use within this course.
units.frag_start: AI is not permitted for any use
units.fit_note: Also one of the named tiers (P05).

units.why: The closed statement says 'Students are expected to do all coursework themselves'. That is an own-work requirement; P29 (students own what they submit) fits better than P19 since it does not mention generation.

documents.title: Faculty Handbook - AI in Higher Education (introduces Policy 220)
documents.stance_why: The page sets no AI-use stance itself: it introduces Policy 220 as 'authoritative' and points to syllabus statements and resources. The rule text is elsewhere, so the stance is delegates.
documents.summary: Handbook page introducing Policy 220, the state-mandated AI policy for instruction and assignments, without reproducing its rules. It lists the AI Task Force outcomes, AI Academy, MInDS Center and syllabus statements.

units.why: States the university's commitment to equip students, faculty and staff to use generative AI: 'committed to ensuring its students, faculty, and staff stay up-to-date and are equipped'. An institutional preamble of purpose (P56); it also speaks of utilizing AI well, mildly encouraging.
units.anchor: Tennessee Tech is committed to ensuring its students, faculty, and staff stay up-to-date
units.frag_start: As generative AI continues to evolve
units.fit_note: Also commits to equipping the community with knowledge and resources to use generative AI.

units.why: Reports a state-law mandate that institutions adopt an AI policy for 'students, faculty, and staff' and post it by July 1, 2025. This explains why the policy exists; it is a legal requirement (P77).
units.anchor: institutions must adopt a policy
units.frag_start: Pursuant to T.C.A. 49-8-203(a); T.C.A. 49-7-185, institutions must adopt
units.policy: Under T.C.A. 49-8-203(a) and 49-7-185, institutions must adopt a policy regarding the use of AI technology by students, faculty and staff for instructional and assignment purposes, and post it on the institutional website by July 1, 2025.
units.fit_note: A state-law requirement to adopt and post an AI policy, rather than a rule on AI use itself.

units.why: Says Policy 220 'outlines' instructional and assignment use of AI and contains task-force recommendations. It describes what the policy is and where it comes from, which is how the policy was made (P84).
units.anchor: includes recommendations from the AI Task Force as well as refers to existing policies relevant
units.frag_start: outlines Tennessee Tech's instructional
units.fit_note: Also says the policy refers to existing policies relevant to AI use.

units.why: Says Policy 220 'is Tennessee Tech's authoritative resource and takes precedence over any information provided on this website'. It sets the hierarchy among sources; nearest is P80 (who owns the policy), but no type matches exactly.
units.anchor: takes precedence over any information provided on this website
units.frag_start: is Tennessee Tech's authoritative resource and
units.uncovered_note: Declares the formal policy authoritative and overriding any guidance on the website.

units.why: Names a contact for questions: 'contact Associate Provost, Dr. Bedelia Russell'. It names who handles questions about the AI policy (P80).
units.anchor: For questions about this policy, contact Associate Provost
units.frag_start: For questions about this policy, contact
units.fit_note: Names a contact for questions rather than an enforcing body.

units.why: Says syllabus statements, integrity-policy revisions and CITL resources 'are in place already to assist faculty and students with AI use'. Pointing faculty and students to support resources fits P63 partly, since it also covers students.
units.anchor: syllabus statements, revisions to the Academic Integrity policy, and CITL resources are in place already
units.frag_start: In addition, syllabus statements, revisions
units.frag_end: faculty and students with AI use for instruction and assignments.
units.fit_note: Supports faculty and students, not faculty only.

units.why: Announces the AI Academy, 'an online asynchronous course designed for anyone looking to explore and build a foundational understanding of Artificial Intelligence'. AI training offered to the community: P70.

units.why: Describes the MInDS Center that 'coordinates artificial intelligence and data science research and education efforts across Tennessee Tech'. An institutional AI coordinating body; nearest P56 but it is a fact about a center, not a framework, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: coordinates artificial intelligence and data science research and education efforts across Tennessee Tech University
units.frag_start: The Machine Intelligence and Data Science Center
units.uncovered_note: Describes a CS-department center that coordinates AI and data science research and education across the university.

units.why: Reports that a 2023 task force reviewed the misconduct policy 'to add information regarding the role of generative AI in academic misconduct'. Treats AI misuse as a matter for the integrity policy (P36) and records how it was made.
units.anchor: to add information regarding the role of generative AI in academic misconduct
units.frag_start: a group was established to review Policy 217
units.fit_note: Also records that the integrity policy was revised by a task force to cover generative AI.

units.why: Notes that Policy 217 has been replaced by Policy 216 Student Academic Integrity. A record of how the policy changed over time, matching P84 (how the policy was made) more than any rule.

units.why: Describes a 2023 AI Task Force from across campus established 'to collect information and propose ideas for the integration of AI on campus'. How and by whom the guidance was developed: P84.

units.why: States that syllabus statements 'are provided for faculty along with the recommended' syllabus template updated each semester. The university provides AI statements for syllabi, a syllabus-communication support (P09 is closest but it is an offer).
